rules.statement: Do not hard-code per-key-type JWK rules (RFC 7638 thumbprint members, private member names) in a `switch` on `kty` or a fixed set; take them from registered key-type data that the key object carries, so contributed key types work too.
rules.why: Hard-coded tables only know the standard key types, so a contributed `kty` could not be thumbprinted and DPoP validation threw `NotSupportedException` even though the catalog could import and export the key.
rules.check: Look for new or changed `switch`/dictionary/set literals keyed on `kty` values ("RSA", "EC", "OKP", "oct", "AKP") that drive thumbprint, private-material or public-key logic, instead of reading the key's registered descriptor.

rules.statement: Attach extensible per-type rules to the object they describe, not to method overloads that make every caller look the rules up again, so an object that crosses a boundary (for example a DPoP proof's public key) keeps its rules.
rules.why: With overloads, every caller has to find the descriptor again, and a key handed across a boundary loses its rules.
rules.check: Look for new overloads such as `Method(descriptor)` that callers can only use after looking up type data the object could have carried itself.

rules.statement: Do not add a static mutable registry for an open vocabulary; register the data through the existing catalog or registry service.
rules.why: Global mutable state causes registration-order and test-isolation problems, and it duplicates the registry that already exists.
rules.check: Look for static mutable collections or static `Register` methods that hold vocabulary entries such as key types or algorithms.

rules.statement: When detecting JWK private key material, fail closed: always treat every standard private member name (`d`, `p`, `q`, `dp`, `dq`, `qi`, `oth`, `k`, `priv`) as private, in addition to the key type's own private members.
rules.why: A contributed key type must not be able to use a standard private name for a public member, and checks such as rejecting an RSA key that carries `k` must still hold.
rules.check: Check that private-material detection or public-key stripping does not rely only on the key type's own list and does not drop any of the standard private member names.

rules.statement: A JWK thumbprint's member set must always include `kty` (RFC 7638 §3.2), and its members must be sorted in ordinal (lexicographic) order (RFC 7638 §3.3).
rules.why: RFC 7638 requires these, and normalizing them where the member set is built keeps thumbprints correct for every key type.
rules.check: Check thumbprint member lists and the canonical JSON built from them: `kty` must be present, and members must be ordered with `StringComparer.Ordinal` rather than culture-sensitive or insertion order.

rules.statement: An AKP key's thumbprint members must be `alg`, `kty` and `pub` (RFC 9964 §6), and AKP keys must always export `alg` and require it on import.
rules.why: RFC 9964 §6 defines these members, and the earlier list without `alg` produced non-conforming thumbprints.
rules.check: Check AKP thumbprint member lists for a missing `alg`, and AKP import/export code that treats `alg` as optional.

rules.statement: A JWK constructor that takes an explicit key-type descriptor must throw `ArgumentException` when the descriptor's name differs from the key's `kty`.
rules.why: A key must not carry rules for a different key type than its own `kty`.
rules.check: Check constructors or factories that pair a JWK with type rules for a missing check that the descriptor name equals `kty`.
